guide.summary: Notion uses OAuth 2.0 only for public connections, which you create in the Developer portal. The flow is a standard authorization code flow for a confidential client, and refresh tokens rotate on every refresh. No review is needed to use a public connection. Notion's security review applies only if you want an optional Marketplace listing, with a stated response time of 5-10 business days. The main trap is the installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only), which you cannot change after creation. Choosing Selected workspaces also rules out a Marketplace listing.
auth_alternatives: Personal access token: choose it for scripts or tools that act as you. There is no OAuth flow, and the token carries the creating user's permissions, so it does not work for letting other users connect their own Notion.

Internal connection token: choose it for team-owned automations inside one workspace. Only a workspace owner can create one and only workspace admins can access the token, so it does not fit an agent serving many users.
Public connection (OAuth 2.0): this is what Notion recommends when other Notion users need to install your app, which is the case for a multi-user agent.

reasons_to_bring_own: You want your own Notion Marketplace listing. Listing requires your own public connection with Any workspace scope that has passed Notion's security review.
You want to control the connection's configuration yourself: name, redirect URIs, installation scope and capabilities are all set on the connection you create.
build_or_borrow.verdict: Use Composio managed auth to start; you do not need your own app yet because a public connection works without any review, so you can create your own later in about 20 minutes when you want your own branding or a Marketplace listing.

prerequisites.text: A Notion account with a workspace to use as the development workspace, which the create form requires.
Your redirect URI(s) ready before creating the connection. If you configure more than one, your token request must include redirect_uri.
A decision on installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only). It cannot be changed later, and only Any workspace is eligible for the Marketplace.
A decision on which capabilities the connection needs, since the create form requires them.

redirect_uri_rules: Redirect URIs are configured on the connection in the Developer portal.
If several redirect URIs are configured, redirect_uri is required in the token request.

blockers.text: Installation scope is fixed at creation. Choosing Selected workspaces only permanently rules out a Marketplace listing for that connection.
blockers.workaround: Pick Any workspace unless you are certain the app stays private. If you chose wrong, you have to create a new connection.

blockers.text: Notion can restrict a connection's API access. A 429 response with public_api_request_blocked will not clear on retry.
blockers.workaround: Detect this error code separately from normal rate limiting, stop retrying, and contact Notion support.

blockers.text: Rate limits apply per connection: 180 requests per minute on most plans and 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise plans.
blockers.workaround: Add backoff and queuing in the agent so it does not burst past the limit.

app_specific_gotchas.text: Installation scope (Any workspace or Selected workspaces only) cannot be changed after the connection is created.
There is no workspace-wide admin approval. Every user must complete the OAuth flow individually.
Each refresh returns a new refresh token as well as a new access token. Store the new one every time or later refreshes will break. Token lifetimes are not documented.
The token endpoint uses HTTP Basic auth with the client ID and secret, which makes this a confidential client. PKCE is not mentioned, so do not rely on a secretless public-client flow.
Marketplace listing details (name, description, category, tags, images, logo) live in a separate Listings section, not in the OAuth configuration.

steps.title: Pick the credential type: public connection (OAuth)
steps.detail_md:
Notion has three credential types: internal connection tokens, personal access tokens, and public connections. **Only public connections use OAuth 2.0.** Notion's own guidance:

- Use a PAT for tools that act as you.
- Use an internal connection for team-owned automations.
- Use a public connection when other Notion users need to install the app.

An agent whose users connect their own Notion needs a **public connection**. PATs act as the creating user, and internal tokens are admin-only, so neither fits multi-user use.

The agent can lay out this comparison, but the developer makes the call. If you use Composio, its Notion toolkit lists managed auth as available, which may let you skip running your own app. Check that separately.

steps.title: Decide installation scope (irreversible)
steps.detail_md:
The create form asks for an installation scope: **Any workspace** or **Selected workspaces only**. It is set at creation and **cannot be changed afterward**. Only Any workspace connections can ever be listed on the Marketplace.

Recommendation: pick **Any workspace** if you might ever want a listing or broad distribution. Pick Selected workspaces only if you are certain the app stays with a known set of workspaces.

The agent can lay out this trade-off. Only the developer can make this decision.

steps.title: Prepare form inputs: name, redirect URIs, capabilities
steps.detail_md:
The agent drafts the inputs the create form requires:

- connection name
- development workspace to use
- redirect URI(s), meaning your production and local callback URLs
- capabilities you need

The specific capability names are not covered here, so read them off the form rather than guessing. If you register more than one redirect URI, your token request must include `redirect_uri`.

steps.title: Create the public connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail_md:
Log in and open the Connections section of the Notion Developer portal (`https://app.notion.com/developers/connections` responded with 200 in a probe). Create a public connection using the inputs from step 3 and the scope chosen in step 2.

The workspace-owner requirement is documented for **internal** connections. Whether creating a public connection needs specific workspace permissions is not documented here.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into your secret store
steps.detail_md: After creation, the OAuth client ID and client secret are on the connection's **Configuration** tab. This is a confidential client: the secret is used server-side for token requests, so keep it out of any frontend.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail_md:
The agent writes the integration code.

- **Authorize:** redirect users to `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize`. `response_type` and `owner` take fixed values. A probe shows the authorize URL forwarding to an install page with `response_type=code`. Take the exact `owner` value from Notion's docs, as it is not given here.
- **Token exchange:** POST to `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token` with HTTP Basic auth (client ID and secret). Send `redirect_uri` if several are registered. PKCE is not mentioned, so do not rely on it.
- **Refresh:** use the same token endpoint. Refresh returns a new access token **and** a new refresh token, so always persist the new refresh token. Token lifetimes are not documented.
- **No discovery:** there are no OIDC or OAuth discovery documents on notion.so, so hardcode the endpoints.

steps.title: Add rate-limit and block handling
steps.detail_md:
Budget requests per connection:

- **600 requests per minute** on Business and Enterprise plans.
- **180 requests per minute** on all other plans.

Back off and retry on ordinary 429s. A 429 with `public_api_request_blocked` means Notion has restricted the connection: do **not** retry. Surface the error and have the developer contact Notion support.

steps.title: Test end to end with your own Notion account
steps.detail_md: Run the full flow against your development workspace: authorize, exchange the code, call the API, then refresh. Every user must complete the OAuth flow individually. No workspace-wide admin approval is described, so design onboarding around a per-user connect step.

steps.title: Ship to users without a Marketplace listing
steps.detail_md:
Listing is optional. A public connection can be used without listing, and users can install it within its installation scope by going through your connect flow. This is the point where the integration is working and shareable.

The security review only gates the **Marketplace listing**, not unlisted use.

steps.title: Optional: draft Marketplace listing content
steps.detail_md:
Only possible if the scope is **Any workspace**. Listing details are managed in the **Listings** section, separate from the OAuth setup. The agent drafts:

- name
- description
- category
- tags
- images
- logo

It also notes which connection to associate.

steps.title: Optional: submit listing and pass security review
steps.detail_md: Log in, enter the listing in the Listings section and submit. Public connections must pass a Notion security review before they can be listed. What the review checks is not documented here.

steps.title: Optional: wait for Notion's review response
steps.detail_md: A response is expected within **5 to 10 business days**. The estimate below is about 10 business days, roughly two calendar weeks. This is the time to a response, not a guaranteed approval. Further rounds are not documented. Your unlisted integration keeps working while you wait.

belief_diff.topic: Does letting arbitrary users connect require provider review or verification?
belief_diff.prior_belief: No, any Notion workspace can authorize a public integration via OAuth without review, but Marketplace listing requires Notion review.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say public connections must pass a Notion security review before Marketplace listing but can be used without listing, and each user must individually authorize; they do not explicitly state that installs need no review.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Marketplace review typically takes about 2 weeks, while OAuth connections for unlisted public integrations need no approval wait.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say Marketplace review response is expected within 5-10 business days, not about 2 weeks; they do not address an OAuth wait for unlisted connections.

belief_diff.topic: Limits while the app is unapproved
belief_diff.prior_belief: Unlisted public integrations have no cap on the number of workspaces that can install them.
belief_diff.finding: Claims describe installation scope (any workspace or selected workspaces) but do not mention any workspace cap for unlisted integrations either way.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Creating and distributing a Notion public integration is free with no paid requirement.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not mention pricing or fees for creating or distributing public connections.

belief_diff.topic: Key prerequisites (domain, privacy policy, video, business verification)
belief_diff.prior_belief: A public integration requires a company name, logo, a privacy policy URL, and terms URL, but no demo video or business verification.
belief_diff.finding: Claims list Marketplace listing fields (name, description, category, tags, images, logo, associated connection) but do not mention company name, privacy policy URL, terms URL, demo video, or business verification.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS, match exactly with no wildcards, and be registered in the integration settings before the OAuth flow runs.
belief_diff.finding: Claims say redirect URIs are set in the Developer portal and redirect_uri is required in the token request when several are configured; they do not address HTTPS or wildcard rules.
